title: Half of US Workers Thinking About a Backup Career
paragraphs: According to a new survey, many Americans — even if they're happy with their job — are thinking about a "plan B" for their career.
The survey, done by Talker Research, asked 2,000 full-time US workers about their jobs and plans for the future.

Nearly half said they are thinking about another career they could turn to if their current job does not work out — a practice known as "career cushioning." And of those, more than three in four had already started preparing for a possible backup career.

But career cushioning does not mean people are planning to leave their jobs soon. In fact, nine in 10 workers had stayed in the same job for the past two years, and over half believed there was little or no chance they would lose their job or need to find another one in the next two years.

However, many workers said their jobs had changed over the past two years. Among those who had stayed in the same job, nearly half said the way they worked had changed a lot — many had to learn new technologies, take on extra work and deal with changes in the economy.

So what might make workers actually switch to their backup career? The most common reasons were being able to do something they enjoy, having a better lifestyle with less stress, or losing their current job.

But not everyone has a plan B. Just over half hadn't thought about changing careers, with many saying they didn't have the time, felt too old to start again, or did not want to return to an entry-level job.
